newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian prosecutors appeal baby smuggling case.
newsitem.headline: Romanian prosecutors appeal baby smuggling case.

text.p: Romanian prosecutors on Tuesday appealed against a suspended jail term handed down to a Briton convicted of smuggling babies out of Romania and they also demanded his expulsion from the country.
Prosecutor Alina Dumitrescu told Reuters she had launched appeal proceedings in connection with John Boast's 20-month suspended sentence, but gave no further details.
The court in the city of Oradea, near the border with Hungary, has yet to set a date for a hearing.
Dumitrescu had earlier said she would demand Boast's expulsion to prevent any repeat of his offences.

Boast, 46, from Harwood in Lancashire, describes himself as a charity worker and was first charged more than a year ago with smuggling a 15-month-old Romanian Gypsy girl over the border with Hungary to Britain for illegal adoption.

In 1996, he was arrested over a second case -- the purchase for the equivalent of $60 of two-year-old Gypsy girl Viola Szilagy, who was taken out of Romania in June 1995. He was freed after six months in police custody.
